newsitem.title: USA: Samsonite's campaign to focus on 'road warrior'.
newsitem.headline: Samsonite's campaign to focus on 'road warrior'.

text.p: Samsonite Corp., the world's leading luggage maker, is trading in its 800-pound gorilla for a new $30 million road warrior ad campaign.

The global campaign, called "War Stories," is the first effort from Omnicom Group's TBWA Chiat/Day, of Venice, Calif., which won the business in February. Leo Burnett Co., Chicago, had handled the $15 million account in the United States.

The campaign, which debuted Wednesday, is designed to reposition the Denver-based company as a provider of global travel solutions. Two 30-second spots will roll out later this summer in international markets.

The ads focus on the company's new EZ Cart luggage lines, which combine European styling with a better organised interior and an upright, four-wheel handling system designed to offer greater mobility.

"We're marrying great European styles with American innovation to create what we believe are the best products available in the marketplace," Richard Nicolosi, president and chief executive officer, said.
Since its launch in last September, the EZ Cart has become the leading luggage item in the country, Nicolosi said.
The new positioning replaces Burnett's familiar durability campaign, featuring a gorilla testing the strength of the luggage.

Nicolosi said the new focus on frequent business travelers makes sense because they account for the lion's share of the travel market. The business traveller also purchases 1.6 pieces of luggage per year, compared with the rest of the population, which only buys one piece of luggage every eight to nine years.
"The road warrior is doing all of the travel and consuming all of the luggage. These people want quality of travel," Nicolosi said.

Samsonite's "War Stories" campaign follows in the same vein as United Airlines' new $125 million advertising campaign, launched May 22 from Fallon McElligott, Minneapolis, and Young & Rubicam, New York. Both depict the travails of frequent air travel.

The marketing campaign is the latest step in Nicolosi's efforts to reverse recent losses at the company. Since joining Samsonite in May 1996, Nicolosi has shifted the company to a category management marketing strategy, hiring two senior marketing executives in September to handle the softside and hardside luggage lines. In November, the company underwent a major restructuring, cutting 450 jobs globally.

It then turned to its advertising agencies, consolidating its business at TBWA Chiat/Day in February after a review that included Burnett, DDB Needham Worldwide and McCann-Erickson Worldwide, both New York; and J. Walter Thompson Co., London.
"The consumer advertising campaign is the next logical step to continue to turbo-charge the renaissance of this company into a great one," Nicolosi said.
